request: Meetings with government officials should be logged automatically so we stop losing engagement history.
executive_summary: This release will automate the logging of meetings with government officials in the Government CRM for regional coordinators and project managers, enhancing data quality and user efficiency. Users will receive notifications confirming successful logging, and a designated data steward will oversee the accuracy of logged information. However, clarity on how meeting confirmations will be documented for audit and compliance purposes remains unresolved.

core_commitments.text: Automated logging of meetings with government officials in the CRM system.
User notifications will be sent to confirm successful logging of each meeting.

in_scope.text: The system will automatically log meetings when a user enters meeting details through a designated interface, capturing date, time, attendees, and key discussion points defined as actionable items or decisions made during the meeting.
in_scope.note: The scope was clarified to ensure that key discussion points are defined as actionable items or decisions made during meetings, which will improve consistency in logging.

in_scope.text: Regional coordinators and project managers will be the primary users of the automated logging feature. A designated data steward will be responsible for maintaining the accuracy of logged information, which includes reviewing logs for errors, correcting inaccuracies, and ensuring adherence to data quality standards.
in_scope.note: A designated data steward's role in maintaining the accuracy of logged information was explicitly included to address ownership and accountability issues.

in_scope.text: Users will receive notifications via the system to confirm the logging of their meetings.
All logged meetings will be associated with the relevant government officials' profiles in the CRM.

The system will ensure that only users with appropriate access rights, specifically regional coordinators, project managers, and designated data stewards with Level 2 security clearance or higher, can log meetings involving sensitive or confidential information. These access levels will be determined by the organization's data governance policy.
in_scope.note: Access rights were firmly established to include only regional coordinators and project managers with Level 2 security clearance to manage confidentiality and security concerns.

in_scope.text: The system will archive all confirmations of scheduled meetings, which includes the method of logging confirmation, such as email confirmations or digital acknowledgment by participants, as evidence to maintain compliance.
in_scope.note: The archiving method for meeting confirmations was revised to meet compliance standards for documentation and audits.

out_of_scope.text: The feature will not include automatic logging of informal meetings or conversations, such as phone calls or casual discussions, which will be classified as meetings not requiring prior scheduling or formality.
out_of_scope.note: Clarification on the classification of informal vs. formal meetings was added to prevent misclassifications and ensure accurate records.

out_of_scope.text: Integration with external calendar systems for automatic meeting logging is not included in this release.
User role management and security clearance updates are outside the scope of this release.

assumptions.text: Users will have access to a designated interface for entering meeting details in the CRM, which the proposal depends on.
Meetings must be scheduled and confirmed beforehand by all parties involved for this feature to work effectively.
assumptions.note: Concern over documenting prior meeting confirmations remains due to unresolved clarity on compliance standards.

assumptions.text: The organization has existing policies regarding data sensitivity and confidentiality, which will dictate how meeting details are logged and accessed.

definitions.text: "Automated logging" means the functionality within the CRM that captures meeting details without manual input once the meeting is scheduled and confirmed.
"Meeting details" means the specific information regarding the meeting, including the date, time, attendees (individuals involved), and an outline of key discussion points.

success_criteria.text: At least 90% of scheduled meetings with government officials are successfully logged within 24 hours of the meeting, with a requirement for logged meetings to be reviewed by a designated data steward if not entered within 24 hours, to ensure data quality is maintained.
success_criteria.note: Success criteria now mandates review of meetings logged later than 24 hours to maintain data quality, addressing earlier concerns around data integrity.

open_questions.question: How will the system document the confirmation of scheduled meetings for compliance and audit purposes?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This documentation is essential to demonstrate that meetings occurred as reported, especially under audit scrutiny.
options: Specify a method for documentation (e.g., emails, digital acknowledgments)
Utilize existing confirmation systems within the organization

proposer.text: The specifics regarding how meeting confirmations will be documented for compliance and audit purposes must be defined by the organization as it involves existing policies.

critic.text: This remains unresolved regarding how confirmations will be documented for audits.

tension.summary: The primary tension centered around the clarity of roles concerning data accuracy and security, particularly regarding who can access and log sensitive information. Throughout the discussions, the proposer worked to clarify responsibilities, while the critic raised concerns over potential gaps in data protection protocols, leading to some revisions but leaving an open question regarding compliance documentation.

proposer.worry: The delineation of roles and processes for data correction may evolve as organizational policies are clarified.

critic.worry: Potential for unauthorized access to sensitive meeting details due to the classification of access rights.

issues.failure_scenario: A project manager without the necessary clearance logs a meeting with confidential information that another team should not see, creating a risk of exposure and potential breach of confidentiality agreements.
issues.resolution_test: What specific roles or clearance levels have the authority to log and view meetings with sensitive information?
